quests.question: The venue allows photography ____ a flash is not used during performances.
quests.sentence: The venue allows photography ____ a flash is not used during performances.
quests.hint: No-flash is the formal condition for photography being permitted.
quests.explanation: 'Provided that' sets a formal condition. Photography is permitted PROVIDED THAT one specific rule is respected. This is typical of venue, museum, or theatre policy language - formal, conditional permission.

quests.question: ____ the board's unanimous backing, the CEO feels confident moving forward.
quests.sentence: ____ the board's unanimous backing, the CEO feels confident moving forward.
quests.hint: The unanimous backing is the acknowledged fact that underpins the CEO's confidence.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces an acknowledged fact as the basis for a state or action. 'Given the board's backing' = 'because the board is fully behind this'. The support (premise) justifies the confidence (conclusion).

quests.question: She submitted the application two weeks early ____ it was rejected and she needed to reapply.
quests.sentence: She submitted the application two weeks early ____ it was rejected and she needed to reapply.
quests.hint: Submitting early is a precaution against the possibility of rejection and reapplication.
quests.explanation: 'In case' introduces a precautionary action against a possible negative outcome. She submitted early in case (= as a safeguard against) rejection - if rejected, she would have time to reapply before the deadline.

quests.question: He repeated the instructions twice ____ there was any confusion among the new staff.
quests.sentence: He repeated the instructions twice ____ there was any confusion among the new staff.
quests.hint: Repeating was a precaution against possible confusion - not certainty.
quests.explanation: 'In case' introduces a precautionary repetition. He repeated the instructions in case (= as a safeguard against) any confusion arising. Repetition was not necessary, but it was done as a safeguard.

quests.question: The new policy applies to all employees ____ they joined before the policy was introduced.
quests.sentence: The new policy applies to all employees ____ they joined before the policy was introduced.
quests.hint: Joining before the policy was the only exception - old-timers might be exempt.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' introduces the one exception to an otherwise universal policy. 'Applies to all employees unless they joined before the policy' = 'the only exception is pre-policy staff'. One clear exception.

quests.question: ____ the restructuring is complete, the new reporting lines will come into effect.
quests.sentence: ____ the restructuring is complete, the new reporting lines will come into effect.
quests.hint: The completion of restructuring is the trigger for the new structure to become active.
quests.explanation: 'Now that' expresses a changed state that enables new action. 'Now that restructuring is complete' = 'because restructuring has now been finished'. The completed change (premise) activates the new reporting structure (conclusion).

quests.question: The system records all transactions ____ there is any dispute at a later date.
quests.sentence: The system records all transactions ____ there is any dispute at a later date.
quests.hint: Recording is a precaution against the possibility of future disputes.
quests.explanation: 'In case' introduces the reason for a precautionary system. Records are kept in case (= as a safeguard against) future disputes. This is standard practice for financial and legal compliance.

quests.question: Please label all containers clearly ____ staff can identify them without opening each one.
quests.sentence: Please label all containers clearly ____ staff can identify them without opening each one.
quests.hint: Clear labelling is the action; easy identification without opening is the purpose.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces the intended purpose. 'Label clearly so that staff can identify them' = 'in order to enable easy identification'. The labelling (action) serves the operational efficiency purpose (result).

quests.question: She will take the role ____ she is given full creative control over the project.
quests.sentence: She will take the role ____ she is given full creative control over the project.
quests.hint: Full creative control is her ongoing condition for accepting the role.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' introduces a continuing condition. 'Will take the role as long as she has full creative control' = 'on the continuing condition that creative freedom is guaranteed'. Remove the condition and she will decline.

quests.question: ____ the charity has reached its fundraising target, the project can officially launch.
quests.sentence: ____ the charity has reached its fundraising target, the project can officially launch.
quests.hint: Reaching the target is the event that enables the launch.
quests.explanation: 'Now that' introduces a completed achievement as the basis for a new action. 'Now that the target has been reached' = 'because the fundraising goal has been met'. The achieved target (changed circumstance) makes launching the project possible.

quests.question: The guard checked every bag carefully ____ anyone smuggled in prohibited items.
quests.sentence: The guard checked every bag carefully ____ anyone smuggled in prohibited items.
quests.hint: 'Lest' is the formal connector for precautionary fear in official or literary contexts.
quests.explanation: 'Lest' introduces a formal precautionary purpose. 'Checked bags carefully lest anyone smuggled prohibited items' = 'checked carefully for fear that someone might smuggle something'. 'Lest' is more formal and literary than 'in case'.

quests.question: She arrives at her client's office an hour early ____ she has time to review her notes.
quests.sentence: She arrives at her client's office an hour early ____ she has time to review her notes.
quests.hint: Arriving early is the deliberate action; reviewing notes is the intended result.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces the purpose of the early arrival. 'Arrives early so that she has time to review' = 'in order to have time to review'. The early arrival (action) is planned to enable a specific activity (purpose).

quests.question: He included a glossary at the back ____ readers unfamiliar with the terminology could follow the text.
quests.sentence: He included a glossary at the back ____ readers unfamiliar with the terminology could follow the text.
quests.hint: The glossary serves readers who need help - it was written for their benefit.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces the purpose of including the glossary. 'Included a glossary so that unfamiliar readers could follow' = 'in order to help readers understand the terminology'. The glossary (tool) serves the comprehension goal (purpose).

quests.question: ____ the global supply chain has stabilised, manufacturers can plan production more reliably.
quests.sentence: ____ the global supply chain has stabilised, manufacturers can plan production more reliably.
quests.hint: Supply chain stability is the changed condition that enables better planning.
quests.explanation: 'Now that' expresses the changed external condition as the basis for a new operational possibility. 'Now that the supply chain has stabilised' = 'because stability has now been restored'. Stability (changed circumstance) enables reliable planning.

quests.question: The organisation maintains a legal compliance fund ____ unexpected regulatory fines arise.
quests.sentence: The organisation maintains a legal compliance fund ____ unexpected regulatory fines arise.
quests.hint: The compliance fund is a financial precaution against unexpected fines.
quests.explanation: 'In case' introduces the reason for a financial precaution. The fund exists in case (= as a safeguard against) unexpected regulatory fines. This is standard risk management practice.

quests.question: She works extra hours in the early part of a project ____ she has more flexibility later.
quests.sentence: She works extra hours in the early part of a project ____ she has more flexibility later.
quests.hint: Front-loading work is intentional; flexibility later is the desired outcome.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces the strategic purpose. 'Works extra hours early so that she has more flexibility later' = 'in order to create flexibility in the later stages'. The upfront effort (action) serves the flexibility goal (purpose).

quests.question: The bridge will remain weight-restricted ____ the engineering assessment is completed.
quests.sentence: The bridge will remain weight-restricted ____ the engineering assessment is completed.
quests.hint: Completing the engineering assessment is the only condition for lifting the restriction.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' introduces the sole condition for changing the restriction. 'Will remain restricted unless the assessment is completed' = 'the restriction will only be lifted if the assessment IS completed'. One condition, one outcome.

quests.question: ____ the level of public interest in the case, publishing the full transcript seems justified.
quests.sentence: ____ the level of public interest in the case, publishing the full transcript seems justified.
quests.hint: The high public interest is the acknowledged fact that justifies publication.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces the acknowledged public reality that justifies a decision. 'Given the level of public interest' = 'taking into account how much public attention this case has received'. The interest (premise) justifies the publication (conclusion).

quests.question: The lawyer advised her client not to comment publicly ____ the statement was misrepresented.
quests.sentence: The lawyer advised her client not to comment publicly ____ the statement was misrepresented.
quests.hint: 'Lest' expresses a formal, professional precautionary concern.
quests.explanation: 'Lest' introduces a formal precautionary concern. 'Advised not to comment lest the statement was misrepresented' = 'for fear that comments might be misrepresented'. This is legal advice language - 'lest' is appropriate for formal professional contexts.

quests.question: The project can proceed ____ the planning committee grants formal approval.
quests.sentence: The project can proceed ____ the planning committee grants formal approval.
quests.hint: Formal planning approval is the mandatory condition for the project to proceed.
quests.explanation: 'Provided that' sets the formal regulatory condition. 'Can proceed provided that planning approval is granted' = 'on condition that formal permission is obtained'. This is standard planning and construction process language.

quests.question: ____ the laboratory results have come back negative, the building can be declared safe.
quests.sentence: ____ the laboratory results have come back negative, the building can be declared safe.
quests.hint: Negative lab results are the event that changes the safety status of the building.
quests.explanation: 'Now that' expresses a completed event as the basis for a changed status. 'Now that results are negative' = 'because the results have now confirmed no contamination'. The clear results (changed circumstance) enable the safety declaration.

quests.question: The architect designed wide corridors ____ wheelchair users and parents with pushchairs could navigate easily.
quests.sentence: The architect designed wide corridors ____ wheelchair users and parents with pushchairs could navigate easily.
quests.hint: Wide corridors are designed to achieve a specific accessibility goal.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces the purpose of an architectural design decision. 'Designed wide corridors so that wheelchair users could navigate easily' = 'in order to ensure accessibility for all users'. The design choice (action) serves an inclusion purpose.

quests.question: ____ the company's debt levels, taking on another large loan would be unwise.
quests.sentence: ____ the company's debt levels, taking on another large loan would be unwise.
quests.hint: High debt levels are the acknowledged fact that makes another loan financially risky.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces the financial reality upon which advice is based. 'Given the company's debt levels' = 'taking into account the existing debt'. The current debt situation (premise) informs the financial recommendation (conclusion).

quests.question: She photocopied all the original documents ____ the originals were lost or damaged.
quests.sentence: She photocopied all the original documents ____ the originals were lost or damaged.
quests.hint: Photocopying is a document preservation precaution.
quests.explanation: 'In case' introduces the precautionary motivation for copying. She made copies in case (= as a safeguard against) the originals being lost or damaged. This is standard document management practice.

quests.question: The terms and conditions were drafted clearly ____ all parties understood their exact obligations.
quests.sentence: The terms and conditions were drafted clearly ____ all parties understood their exact obligations.
quests.hint: Clear drafting is the action; universal understanding of obligations is the purpose.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces the purpose of careful legal drafting. 'Drafted clearly so that all parties understood' = 'in order to ensure clarity of obligation for all signatories'. The drafting quality (action) serves the legal clarity goal (purpose).

quests.question: She stored emergency supplies in the basement ____ there was an extended power outage.
quests.sentence: She stored emergency supplies in the basement ____ there was an extended power outage.
quests.hint: Emergency supplies are a household precaution against possible power outages.
quests.explanation: 'In case' introduces the precautionary reason for storing emergency supplies. She stored them in case (= as a safeguard against) an extended power cut. Not expected, but prepared for.

quests.question: ____ the two teams have agreed on a shared framework, collaboration will be much smoother.
quests.sentence: ____ the two teams have agreed on a shared framework, collaboration will be much smoother.
quests.hint: Reaching agreement is the event that changes the collaboration dynamic.
quests.explanation: 'Now that' expresses the achieved agreement as the basis for a new, better situation. 'Now that they have agreed on a framework' = 'because agreement has now been reached'. The agreement (changed circumstance) enables smoother collaboration.

quests.question: The public health authority issued clear guidelines ____ citizens could protect themselves effectively.
quests.sentence: The public health authority issued clear guidelines ____ citizens could protect themselves effectively.
quests.hint: Issuing guidelines is the action; enabling self-protection is the purpose.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces the public health purpose. 'Issued guidelines so that citizens could protect themselves' = 'in order to enable the public to take effective protective action'. The guidelines (tool) serve the public health goal (purpose).

quests.question: The contract included a penalty clause ____ either party attempted to withdraw early.
quests.sentence: The contract included a penalty clause ____ either party attempted to withdraw early.
quests.hint: The penalty clause is a contractual precaution against early withdrawal.
quests.explanation: 'In case' introduces the reason for a contractual safeguard. The penalty clause exists in case (= as a safeguard against) either party withdrawing early. The clause deters withdrawal rather than assuming it will happen.

quests.question: ____ the pilot scheme has demonstrated clear benefits, scaling it nationally makes sense.
quests.sentence: ____ the pilot scheme has demonstrated clear benefits, scaling it nationally makes sense.
quests.hint: Demonstrated benefits are the changed situation that justifies scaling up.
quests.explanation: 'Now that' expresses the achieved result as the basis for logical next steps. 'Now that the pilot has demonstrated benefits' = 'because the pilot has now proved its value'. The proven success (changed circumstance) justifies national scaling.
